newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares higher, dollar loses ground.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares higher, dollar loses ground.

text.p: European shares gained ground in morning trading on Thursday, with the London and Paris markets up half a percent or more although Frankfurt lost much of its early advance.
On the currency market the dollar drifted lower as thin pre-Easter trading exaggerated movements. It was more than a pfennig and over half a yen below late European levels on Wednesday.
"There's actually not much trade going through in spite of the price moves. That didn't take more than just a few major sellers," said a currency trader at a German bank.

Traders in London, the biggest European stock market, reported pre-holiday caution amid uncertainty over higher interest rates and the British election campaign. The market will be closed on Friday and Monday.

Shares were, however, underpinned by "bed and breakfast" tax-related trading near the end of the fiscal year on April 5. But many market participants were absent ahead of the long Easter weekend break.
"We've seen a lot of bed and breakfast deals this morning," one senior dealer said. "Market makers are also trying to squeeze out a few bears ahead of the(tax)year end."
Bed and breakfast transactions, which involve selling shares and then immediately buying them back ahead of the end of the tax year, are used to book capital gains or losses for tax purposes.
Traders still at work are already fretting about the next tightening of American monetary policy after this week's quarter percentage point interest rate rise.
Analysts speculate that the Federal Reserve could boost U.S. rates again in May to keep a lid on inflation.
Meanwhile, the diary has little in the way of corporate news or economic data to whip up enthusiasm.
The key FTSE-100 index of British blue-chip share prices has gained around 86 points or two percent over the past two sessions but Wall Street gave little new lead overnight.

"The Dow is still looking vulnerable. The Street was hoping that the Fed rate hike would be the last for awhile but now people are talking about another quarter-point hike in May," one London dealer said.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.53 points to 6,880.70 on Wednesday, while the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index jumped 21.02 points to 1,269.08.
In Frankfurt, shares were led higher by car companies, partly catching up with gains in later electronic trade on Wednesday.
But then a further dip in the dollar, unhelpful news for German exporters, helped trim gains.
Stronger bond markets helped French shares revive after opening marginally weaker, with healthy company results giving support.
But Paris traders said trading was likely to be affected by the expiry during the day of March futures and options.
For the dollar, meanwhile, concern over Japan's large trade surplus and disappointment that it failed to gain more after Tuesday's rate rise were depressants.

"The dollar had a good go at the upside this week as a lot of people bought dollars ahead of the Fed meeting and the rate hike. Then nothing much happened afterwards so it's coming off a bit," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The U.S. currency slipped against the yen in Asian business after concern expressed by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers about Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"The dollar's slipped a bit on the Summers comment but it's very quiet in Europe with the holidays beckoning," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Summers said Washington had frequently expressed concern about the "dangerous possibility" that the Japanese current account surplus would expand substantially.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will visit Japan on April 4 for talks in which the nagging trade tensions are expected to feature prominently.
On the data front, U.S. weekly jobless claims at 1330 GMT provide what interest there is, followed by U.S. February home sales at 1500 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6780 marks and 123.55 yen, compared with 1.6920 and 124.16 in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 29.0 points, or 0.67 percent, at 4,330.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 13.13 points or 0.50 percent ahead at 2,661.86.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 3.40 points, or 0.10 percent, at 3,421.52.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed in the morning at $349.50 an ounce, up from $346.05 on Wednesday afternoon and the previous London close of $348.75, before slipping back to around $348.85 in quiet trading. Silver was one cent weaker at $5.14.
